rationale: The bug is the use of the `is` operator instead of the `==` operator to compare integer values. In CPython, integers in the range [-5, 256] are cached as singletons, so `is` will work correctly for them. However, for integers outside this range, new objects may be created for the same value, causing `is` to return `False` even when the values are equal. This violates the contract which requires correct comparison for any integer.
